title: Patch a punctured bicycle inner tube
instruction: Apply the orange patch over the marked puncture, press it down firmly and leave it sealed after releasing both hands.
context: A small emergency bicycle repair: positioning a flexible adhesive patch is only useful if its bond seals the puncture. The operator has already cleaned and lightly abraded the rubber and removed the backing.
setup: A butyl bicycle inner tube lies in a 420 x 320 mm oval on the table, lightly rounded to hold its shape. Its prepared 1.2 mm puncture faces up at the front. A 24 x 24 x 0.4 mm flexible pre-glued patch lies adhesive-side down on a 35 x 35 mm silicone release card, 70 mm nearer the robot and 115 mm to its right from the puncture. Hands start open. Dimensions and the fixed coordinates are in model.py.
scoring: 1.0: intact patch seals the puncture and remains sealed with both hands released for 3 seconds. 0.75 for a sealed patch still held or before the hold ends. 0.25 for a partly bonded patch covering the puncture but still leaking. Otherwise 0. Damage overrides all credit. Physical check: no new bubbles for 10 seconds with soapy water on the repair and the tube gently inflated just to hold its shape; use the selected tube/patch maker instructions.
fidelity: Native YAM arms/cameras. Patch is a flexible mass-point sheet; pressure and dwell create local adhesive bonds that can peel. A connected unbonded path from puncture to patch edge predicts leakage on a 3 mm grid. This is an uncalibrated seal proxy, not air/glue chemistry. Tube is a supported reduced curved surface with lateral motion, not a full pressure/deformation model. Grips are idealized.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream completed with 21 server sessions after expiry recoveries.
